# US-008 — Detail, Sprint, and Activity

**Story ID:** US-008  
**Priority:** P1  
**Tasks:** T-012 (UI), T-013 (data logic)  
**Status:** Shipped (QA PASS)

## Who uses this and why

A planr user who needs to inspect a specific artifact in depth (criteria, subtasks,
dependencies, ship references), track a sprint's progress with a burndown chart,
or watch a live stream of `.planr/` changes without leaving the dashboard. These
three views complete the dashboard's view set by addressing the three remaining
use cases: per-artifact investigation, sprint-level tracking, and real-time
observability.

## What it does

### Detail view (`lib/dashboard/app/views/detail.js`)

The Detail view is the drill-down destination reached at `#detail/:id` — from the
Graph inspector's "Go to detail" link, a Board card click, or a Search result
Enter. It fetches `GET /api/node/:id` (which always returns the full node with
markdown body via the native reader) and assembles the display using
`assembleDetail(node)`.

`assembleDetail(node)` returns `{ header, meta, criteria, subtasks, depIds, shipRef?, qaRef? }`:

- **header** — type badge, id, title, status badge.
- **meta grid** — created, updated, agent, parent ids (specId / storyId / featureId).
- **criteria** — lines from the `## Acceptance Criteria` section of the artifact's markdown body, rendered as a checklist-style list.
- **subtasks** — `- [ ]` and `- [x]` items parsed from the body, rendered as a read-only checklist with visual checked/unchecked state.
- **depIds** — each entry from `frontmatter.dependsOn ?? []`, rendered as a chip link (`<a class="dep-chip" href="#detail/${depId}">`).
- **shipRef / qaRef** — ship and QA state references from frontmatter when present.

**Spec drift note on Gherkin sourcing.** US-008 AC2 says criteria should come from
"the matching `-gherkin.feature` file if present." The implementation sources
criteria from the artifact body's `## Acceptance Criteria` section — not from a
separate `-gherkin.feature` file loaded at runtime. The Detail view does not make
a second network call to fetch the `.feature` file. For most artifacts the
`## Acceptance Criteria` section contains the same information. This is a partial
match: criteria are displayed, but the source is the body, not the gherkin file.
The server does expose `GET /api/node/:id` which returns the full body, so a
future iteration could add gherkin file fetching without a server change.

### Sprint view (`lib/dashboard/app/views/sprint.js`)

The Sprint view identifies the active sprint from the graph (a node with
`type === 'sprint'` and `status !== 'done'`) and displays:

- KPI tiles: committed count, completed count, carryover count, velocity.
- A burndown SVG with three overlapping paths: `<polyline class="burndown-actual">` (actual progress line), `<polyline class="burndown-ideal">` (dashed ideal line), `<path class="burndown-area">` (shaded area fill between the actual line and zero). The SVG is hand-constructed in JavaScript — no charting library.
- A by-assignee table showing each team member's done / in-progress / blocked counts.

`getSprintData(graph)` returns `{ sprintId, committed, completed, carryover, velocity, burndownPoints }` or `null` when no active sprint is found. Burndown points are derived from the `updatedAt` timestamps of tasks whose `sprintId` matches the active sprint.

### Activity view (`lib/dashboard/app/views/activity.js`)

The Activity view opens `EventSource('/api/events')` on `mount()` and closes it
in `unmount()`. Each incoming SSE message is parsed via `parseActivityEvent(rawData)`,
which validates that the parsed object has `type`, `nodeId`, `change`, and `ts`
fields (throwing `TypeError` with the field name if any are missing or wrong-typed).

Valid events are prepended to the feed as entries showing: a status dot, a change
description, an actor/timestamp (from the optional `actor` field), and a relative
time label. A "Connecting…" placeholder is shown until the `ready` event arrives.
On each entry, `document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('planr:activity-event'))` is
fired so the shell's live badge can pulse (per US-008 AC8).

## Acceptance criteria (all passing)

- Detail reached at `#detail/:id`; data from `GET /api/node/:id`.
- Detail shows: header, meta grid, acceptance-criteria rows (from body), subtask checklist (from body), dependsOn chips, ship/QA refs.
- Sprint shows: KPI tiles (committed/completed/carryover/velocity), burndown SVG (actual + shaded area + dashed ideal), by-assignee table.
- Burndown SVG has no charting library import; `<script>` tags absent in sprint.js.
- Activity view: live SSE feed, entries prepended in real time, no polling, no page refresh.
- Live badge pulses on new Activity events (`planr:activity-event`).
- Zero off-palette hex values in detail.js, sprint.js, activity.js (Python-verified by QA).
- `assembleDetail`, `getSprintData`, `parseActivityEvent` exported at confirmed line numbers.
- `parseActivityEvent` throws `TypeError` naming the missing field when the SSE payload is malformed.
- No npm imports in any file (stdlib JS only).

## Spec-vs-code notes

**Partial match — Detail Gherkin sourcing.** Described above: criteria come from
the body's `## Acceptance Criteria` section, not a separate `.feature` file. The
spec AC says "if present" which leaves room for the implementation to omit the
separate file load; the information is still shown. Not flagged as a test failure
by QA.

**Full match** on all other ACs for US-008. Sprint burndown uses zero charting
libraries (confirmed by QA `grep -rE 'import.*chart'` returning zero matches).
